name: Stack Culling (Parent Node Re-intersection)
definition: A technique to reduce expensive ray-primitive intersections by pushing the parent node onto the short stack instead of its children when multiple children intersect and at least one is a leaf. The parent is re-intersected later to cull children with hit distances greater than the current closest hit.
summary: Stack Culling reduces primitive intersections by pushing the parent node for re-intersection when multiple children hit, trading minor traversal overhead for significant culling gains using only one extra bit per stack entry.
